source_review.notes: Checked all nine structured references at Apache Spark, Dask, Apache Arrow, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hadoop, Apache Parquet, and OpenLineage; every URL returned HTTP 200. Claims about Spark partition/shuffle/spill and adaptive tuning, Dask partitions/divisions, Arrow dataset partition pruning/layout trade-offs, Iceberg hidden/evolving partition specs, Hadoop split/partition/task concepts, Parquet physical hierarchy, and lineage identity match the cited documentation and remain product/version scoped.

Checked bag-union coverage/disjointness, half-open range ownership, homomorphic aggregation, mean state, join fanout, stage lower bound, and manifest acceptance equations for coherent notation.
Draft chapter validation accepted the exact front matter, H1, H2/H3 contract, local links, and GitHub-compatible inline/display math.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Input, execution, shuffle, data/output, file, row-group, attempt, and committed-generation identities remain explicitly separated.

evidence: Executed the annotated finite model: 8 unique events, three-bucket counts (2,3,3), four-bucket counts (3,2,2,1), customer states c1=(2,80), c2=(2,100), c3=(2,25), c4=(1,5), c5=(1,30), and total 240 cents.
Verified three- and four-bucket merged outputs are identical and a manifest selecting one of two partition-1 attempts exposes each expected event ID exactly once.
Recomputed Exercise 2: partition means 0 and 10 average unweighted to 5, while sufficient states (0,1) and (90,9) combine to global mean 90/10=9.
Recomputed Exercise 3: hot-key fanout is 4,000*2,000=8,000,000 potential pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All explicit bucket distributions, occurrence counts, customer totals, mean counterexample, and join cross-product results reproduce exactly.

evidence: Verified bag union of deterministic single-valued partitions encodes both coverage and disjointness at occurrence level, while equal payload values may legitimately remain repeated.
Verified adjacent half-open ranges [b_i,b_i+1) do not share ordinary boundary values and jointly cover the named outer interval under one type/precision and explicit null policy.
Verified mergeable computation requires sufficient state and associative combine; count/sum and (sum,count) mean state qualify, whereas averaging final partition means does not.
Verified stage completion cannot be less than its slowest required partition path under the idealized model and actual scheduling/resource constraints can only add delay.
Verified manifest exactness requires every expected logical partition and one selected attempt, even when extra physical attempts exist.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The deductions state occurrence, boundary, algebra, placement, and attempt-selection premises rather than treating all operations as partition-local.

invariant_checking.notes: The invariants cover source membership through execution placement and physical layout to one trusted generation.

evidence: Reviewed the occurrence-bag partition proof and confirmed counts alone cannot establish identity coverage because one duplicate and one omission can cancel.
Reviewed the partial-aggregation proof and the explicit unequal-partition mean counterexample showing why final local statistics may be insufficient state.
Reviewed the hot-key join argument: equal keys colocate under ordinary hash partitioning, so increasing bucket count does not split the a_k*b_k cross-product.
Reviewed attempt/manifest construction: multiple physical attempts are allowed, but exact logical effects require one selected receipt/object set for every expected partition before publication.
Reviewed the stage-duration maximum as a lower bound, not a complete runtime prediction.
proof_review.notes: Each proof distinguishes logical occurrence semantics, physical placement, empirical resources, and commit reachability.

evidence: Coverage/disjointness explicitly uses bag union and a deterministic single-valued assignment rather than set equality over payload values.
Aggregation equivalence is labeled conditional on sufficient associative state, with separate warnings for floating order and nonlocal operations.
The stage maximum is labeled idealized/lower-bound, and partition/file sizing guidance is empirical rather than universal.
Spark, Dask, Arrow, Iceberg, Hadoop, Parquet, and OpenLineage claims are source-attributed and product/version scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter visibly separates mathematical premises, implementation mechanisms, vendor contracts, performance observations, and operational recommendations.

evidence: The stable teaching hash is explicitly unsuitable as an unqualified production distribution algorithm and is used only to expose arithmetic.
The finite executable model disclaims distributed engines, adversarial hashing, files, shuffles, speculation races, transactions, performance, and production publication.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review establishes occurrence partitioning, mergeable state, skew lower bounds, and manifest selection; exposition progresses from source/assignment semantics through operators, shuffle/join/skew, files/pruning, retries/publication, validation, security, and evolution; the executable model makes repartition/retry invariants concrete; and ten examples plus five solved exercises combine calculation and design.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. References and local checks were performed on 2026-09-02. The finite standard-library model and recomputations do not establish production source-manifest completeness, record-split correctness, hash quality, time-zone/calendar policy, arbitrary operator composability, floating reproducibility, distributed shuffle/join behavior, skew mitigation, resource/partition/file sizing, pruning correctness, table-format commits/evolution, speculative-attempt races, authorization/privacy compliance, lineage completeness, concurrent backfill/compaction safety, atomic publication, garbage collection, rollback, or disaster recovery; those require system-specific deployed evidence.
